subject: RFP: Dedicated Inference Reserve — capacity worksheet & clarifying questions
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecloud.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: RFP Team <rfp@acmecloud.com>, Victor Huang <victor.huang@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP: Dedicated Inference Reserve — capacity worksheet & clarifying questions

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for taking this RFP — attached is our dedicated-reservation worksheet (acme_rfp_dedicated_questions.xlsx). A few clarifying items that would help us complete vendor scoring: 

- We need a recommended GPU mix for a baseline runrate of 75M tokens/day and a peak burst of 300M tokens/day (24h window smoothing ok). Please map throughput to NVIDIA families (A100, H100, GH200 or equivalent) and any quantized variants you support.
- P95 tail latency target: 250–400ms for single-turn text generation; for chat-heavy endpoints we expect up to 800ms P95. Provide latency numbers for both dedicated and fallback mode.
- What are your standard SLA carveouts for scheduled maintenance and model rollouts?
- Does your reservation support regional failover (we expect primary in us-east, DR in us-west)? Impacts on throughput?
- For pricing/commitment tiers we’ll evaluate three horizons: 12, 24, 36 months — please include run-rate economics for each.

Can you return the populated worksheet and a short (1–2 page) capacity summary by Dec 22? We may schedule a technical deep-dive after that.

Thanks — Elena
Procurement Manager, Acme Cloud

Attachment: acme_rfp_dedicated_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet, 78KB)

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated Inference Reserve — capacity worksheet & clarifying questions

Elena —

Thanks for the worksheet. Quick summary attached: redwood_capacity_workbook_v3.xlsx. High-level notes up front:

- Baseline / peak mapping: For your 75M tokens/day baseline we recommend a mix dominated by A100/80GB-class equivalents for cost efficiency and predictable throughput. For peak (300M/day) we recommend a 20% H100-capacity buffer to handle short bursts with lower queuing. We include quantized int8 profiles that improve throughput ~1.6x for chat-style loads.
- Latency: Typical P95 for our dedicated pools at 2048-token contexts: A100-class ~180–240ms, H100-class ~120–170ms (single-turn). Chat endpoints (with KV cache warm) P95 ~300–500ms depending on model length. We included tail simulations per GPU family in the workbook.
- Regional failover: supported; automatic routing increases cross-region latency by ~40–70ms and reduces effective burst capacity by ~15% unless redundant reserved slots are provisioned in both regions.
- SLAs: Standard package: 99.9% availability with 8-hour scheduled maintenance windows quarterly; enterprise SLA available with tighter windows and dedicated runbook.

Questions from our side (to validate workbook assumptions):
1) Is the 300M-token burst a single sustained day peak or repeated multi-day pattern?
2) Are there hard constraints on P99 tail or only P95?
3) Will you accept mixed quantization (int8) for non-sensitive workloads while we keep fp16/higher accuracy variants for sensitive traffic?

Cc'ing Kim and Ben to address GPU-family mapping and pricing band questions. If Dec 22 is tight we can do a short workshop next week to align.

—Sergio
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_capacity_workbook_v3.xlsx (workbook, 240KB)

Elena — quick technical addendum from infra: 

- GPU families: Our A100-class profile assumes 80GB memory, 16–20 TFLOPS FP16 equivalent; H100-class references 80GB NVL and includes sparsity/structural improvements for some models. We also include a GH200-compatible profile for very large context runs — note throughput per-card varies by model and tokenizer.
- Fallback SKUs: If you want lower-cost standby capacity, we can map to 48GB A10-style instances for best-effort burst; these reduce tail consistency and should be paired with autoscaling policies.
- Cache warmup: For chat workloads we recommend prefix-KV warming; our workbook models warm and cold starts separately.

Ben — can you add the 24/36-month pricing bands into page 3 of the workbook and produce an alternate scenario with 50% int8 adoption?

Thanks,
Kim
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmecloud.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 11:04:00 -0800

Thanks for the quick responses and the workbook. Couple follow-ups after internal scoring: 

- Burst pattern: 300M/day is a likely single-day spike tied to release events; we expect those ~6–8 times per year, not sustained multi-day.
- P99: we do track P99 for latency-sensitive endpoints — for a subset of traffic we require P99 < 1.2s.
- Security: certain workloads (PII and billing) cannot use lower-precision quantized variants; we will label traffic buckets.

We’d like to set a short architecture workshop (60 minutes) in the week of Jan 4 to walk through the workbook, failure modes, and a proposed canary plan for a pilot (20% of production traffic). Available slots: Jan 4 10:00–12:00 PST or Jan 5 14:00–16:00 PST. Can you confirm?

Regards,
Elena
Procurement Manager, Acme Cloud

3) Canary plan: pilot traffic split, rollbacks, and observability gates (15m)

Deliverables before the call: updated workbook with 24/36-month pricing bands and a one-page canary-runbook (attached: canary-plan-template.pdf). Post-call we’ll provide a short decision memo and an optional addendum covering P99 hardening strategies.
